## Summary

### The Bug

The Redis `SUBSTR`/`GETRANGE` command returned the wrong result when `start` was `0` (or a large negative value clamped to `0`) and `end` was a negative number that, after index conversion, still pointed *before* the start of the string.

For example, with `test = "cat"` (length 3):
- `SUBSTR test 0 -500` returned `"c"` instead of `""`
- `SUBSTR test -5000 -500` returned `"c"` instead of `""`

### Root Cause

In `getrangeCommand` (`src/t_string.c`), the negative-index conversion logic was:

```c
if (start < 0) start = strlen+start;
if (end < 0) end = strlen+end;
if (start < 0) start = 0;
if (end < 0) end = 0;          // <-- BUG
if ((unsigned long long)end >= strlen) end = strlen-1;
```

When `end = -500` and `strlen = 3`, after `end = strlen+end` we get `end = -497`, which is still negative. The line `if (end < 0) end = 0;` then clamped it to `0` (the first character). With `start = 0`, the final check `start > end` became `0 > 0` (false), so the first character was wrongly returned.

This clamping lost the information that `end` pointed *before* the string, meaning the requested range is entirely outside the string and should be empty.

### The Fix

I replaced the `if (end < 0) end = 0;` clamp with an explicit empty-string return when `end` is still negative after conversion:

```c
if (end < 0) {
    /* If end is still negative after the conversion above it means that
     * it points before the start of the string, so the requested range is
     * entirely outside of the string and an empty string must be returned. */
    addReply(c,shared.emptybulk);
    return;
}
```

### Verification

- Built Redis and confirmed the bug was reproduced before the fix and resolved after.
- Ran a comprehensive set of 35 manual test cases (including the bug cases and all existing test expectations) â all pass.
- Ran a 5000-iteration fuzzing comparison against a reference implementation (including negative indices) â 0 mismatches.
- Ran the official Redis test suite for `unit/type/string` (and `unit/limits`) â all tests pass, including `GETRANGE` tests, `GETRANGE fuzzing`, and `Coverage: SUBSTR`.
